transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you into the clinic today?

I’m here because I can’t stop rechecking my spreadsheets and calculations. I’ll go over the same numbers again and again, even after I know I’ve checked them. Sometimes I stay at work for hours after everyone else leaves because I feel like if I don’t check one more time, something bad will happen and it’ll be my fault.
Do you find yourself doing similar repetitive checking or routines in other parts of your life, such as at home?

Mostly it’s the checking that takes over at work. I keep going back through the spreadsheets and calculations, even when I know I already checked them. I’ll stay for hours after everyone’s gone because I feel like I have to do it one more time, or something bad could happen and it would be my fault.
Aside from your concerns about work, do you find yourself constantly worrying about many other everyday topics, like your health, family, or finances?
Not really. I mean, I have normal things I think about, but it’s not like I’m constantly worrying about lots of different areas. It’s mainly the work checking that I can’t let go of.
Deep down, does this repetitive checking feel excessive or senseless to you, or does it feel like the right and necessary way to ensure work is done correctly?
I know I’ve already checked, and part of me knows it’s too much. But it still feels necessary. If I leave without checking again, I feel like something will go wrong and it’ll be my fault.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F60.5 as the repetitive checking is driven by obsessional doubt and anxiety about harm/responsibility, and recognized as excessive, characteristic of obsessive-compulsive disorder rather than obsessive-compulsive personality disorder.
